newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: No Bally decision expected from Oerlikon.
newsitem.headline: No Bally decision expected from Oerlikon.

text.p: Shoes-to-guns manufacturer Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG said its board of directors would not take a decision later on Monday at a meeting on turnaround plans for shoes and fashion unit Bally.
"It is purely a presentation meeting. No decisions and no statements are planned," Oerlikon spokeswoman Yvonne Buechel told Reuters.
Oerlikon's board was meeting to interview Bally chief executive Ernst Thomke, who has publicly threatened to resign if his demand for a new cash infusion for Bally is not met.

Thomke, a renowned turnaround specialist in Switzerland who took over at Bally in September 1995, was due to inform the board concerning the status of his restructuring efforts at Bally and his further plans.

Disagreements between Thomke and Oerlikon's board were made public after Thomke told reporters in May that Bally needed around 150 million Swiss francs in additional funds for restructuring, including remodelling and relocating Bally shops worldwide.
Hortense Anda-Buerhle, the dominant Buehrle family shareholder and a board member, criticised Thomke for suggesting a Bally spin-off to raise the extra money.
In late July, Oerlikon chairman Hans Widmer issued a statement ruling out the possibility of spinning off Bally.
Thomke then responded in a newspaper interview, saying he was disappointed with Widmer because they had agreed not to make any statements about Bally until after the August 18 meeting.
